speaker: Doctor
text: That's an unusual start—let me clarify your symptoms. Can you describe the nature of the swelling and pain in your right ring finger, and how quickly it has progressed?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds like a significant injury. Did you hear a "pop" or "snap" at the moment of the injury, and is the finger currently deformed or deviated? Also, can you extend or flex your finger on its own without assistance?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pyelonephritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
There seems to be a significant confusion; Pyelonephritis is a kidney infection and cannot cause localized finger swelling or deformity. Given your history of hyperextension during football, did you notice an audible "snap" or "pop" when the injury occurred?

REQUEST TEST: X-Ray_Right_Hand (lateral view) to assess for joint dislocation or avulsion fracture.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: X-Ray of the Right Hand (Lateral View): No bone fractures or dislocations visible. Soft tissue swelling noted around the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the X-ray; it rules out a fracture or dislocation, but we still need to determine if there is soft tissue damage to the flexor tendon. When you try to make a fist, can you bend your other fingers normally while your ring finger stays straight?

REQUEST TEST: MRI_Right_Hand (focused on flexor digitorum profundus tendon)
REQUEST IMAGES: Please provide ultrasound images of the flexor tendons in the right ring finger to assess for a rupture.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet Finger (Avulsion of the Extensor Tendon at the Distal Phalanx)

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
